newsitem.title: UK: UK's Channel 5 to delay launch by 4-6 weeks.
newsitem.headline: UK's Channel 5 to delay launch by 4-6 weeks.

text.p: Britain's fifth terrestrial television channel said on Wednesday it was likely to delay its planned January 1 launch by some four to six weeks.
Channel 5 spokeswoman Sally Osman said the new channel would definitely not make the January 1 date and that the delay "may be four to six weeks".

Channel 5 said the delay followed the granting of access earlier this week to a new frequency which would make the channel available in an extra 1.8 million homes -- boosting total coverage to over 80 percent of the UK.
The extra coverage created more work for Channel 5's engineers who were visiting millions of households nationwide to retune video recorders in order to prevent interference from the new channel.
"We want to make sure we get everything right," said Osman, stressing that Channel 5 wanted to complete the retuning process before it goes on air.
Under the original plan, the Independent Television Commission (ITC) watchdog specified that 90 percent of the retuning had to be completed before the channel began broadcasting.
Osman said that Channel 5 would have to redraft its retuning plan following the expansion of the number of homes it could reach and that it did not have a specific revised target date for the launch.
She said Channel 5 would be consulting the ITC about the delay but denied that there had been problems with the retuning process itself so far.
Channel 5 Broadcasting is a consortium comprising British media companies Pearson and United News & Media plus broadcast group CLT of Luxembourg and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
Pearson said recently that the retuning process would cost some 100 million stg. That was before the extra 1.8 million households were added to the budget.
Critics of the retuning plan have dubbed it a "thieves' charter" and the British Retail Consortium has voiced concern that it could invalidate product guarantees.
